title: Smooth locus of a flat locally finitely presented algebraic-space morphism
statement: Algebraic spaces and their etale scheme charts are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts by [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Fibre products and geometric fibres use [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces. Smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a largest open subspace $U_f\subseteq X$ on which $f$ is smooth. For every scheme morphism $g:T\to S$, the smooth locus of $f_T:X\times_ST\to T$ is the inverse image of $U_f$. For each point $s\in S$, $(U_f)_s$ is exactly the smooth locus of $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. These assertions hold for arbitrary field extensions of $\kappa(s)$ and for empty fibres.
